implementation_notes: In NestJS the layer is a class implementing NestInterceptor whose intercept(context, next) runs around the handler: not calling next.handle() means the handler never executes, and binding it globally (APP_INTERCEPTOR provider or app.useGlobalInterceptors) or per controller with @UseInterceptors makes the chain explicit. Payload validation is the framework's pipe mechanism - a ValidationPipe bound with @UsePipes throws before the route handler is invoked, which Nest documents as validation at the system boundary. The DI-managed interceptor replaces manual construction; in a framework-free TypeScript service the same layer is plain middleware, so prefer Nest's form only where the app already runs on Nest.
pitfalls: An interceptor that only wraps the response stream still lets the handler run; rejection must return or throw before next.handle() is called.

Global interceptors registered with useGlobalInterceptors() are instantiated outside the module context, so dependency injection does not work for them - register via APP_INTERCEPTOR when the validator needs injected services.
TypeScript types vanish at runtime: an interface-typed body validates nothing; bind a runtime schema pipe (ValidationPipe/Standard-Schema pipe) or the input stays unchecked.
